# Major Donor Stewardship Plan

## Overview
A comprehensive approach to building lasting relationships with major donors through strategic, personalized engagement.

---

## I. Donor Segmentation

### Tier Definition
- **Leadership Level**: $100,000+
- **Major Gift Level**: $25,000 - $99,999
- **Principal Gift Level**: $10,000 - $24,999
- **Emerging Major Donors**: $5,000 - $9,999

---

## II. Core Stewardship Principles

### The 4 R's
1. **Recognition** - Acknowledge contributions meaningfully
2. **Reporting** - Show impact and outcomes
3. **Relationship** - Build genuine connections
4. **Re-engagement** - Invite continued partnership

---

## III. Stewardship Timeline

### Within 48 Hours
- Personal phone call from executive leadership
- Handwritten thank-you note
- Official tax receipt

### Within 2 Weeks
- Personalized welcome packet
- Assignment of relationship manager
- First impact update

### Months 1-3
- Impact report specific to funded program
- Personal meeting or site visit invitation
- Introduction to program staff/beneficiaries

### Months 4-6
- Mid-year impact update
- Invitation to exclusive event
- Feedback survey or conversation

### Months 7-9
- Personal note with story of impact
- Behind-the-scenes access opportunity
- Strategic planning input opportunity

### Months 10-12
- Comprehensive annual impact report
- Renewal conversation begins
- Recognition event invitation

---

## IV. Engagement Strategies by Tier

### Leadership Level ($100K+)
- Quarterly face-to-face meetings
- Board meeting attendance invitation
- Named recognition opportunities
- Annual private dinner with leadership
- Customized impact reports (quarterly)
- First access to new initiatives
- Personal site visits with program staff

### Major Gift Level ($25K-$99K)
- Semi-annual in-person meetings
- VIP event invitations
- Bi-annual impact reports
- Annual appreciation reception
- Program advisory role opportunities
- Behind-the-scenes tours

### Principal Gift Level ($10K-$24K)
- Annual face-to-face meeting
- Quarterly email updates
- Annual impact report
- Donor appreciation events
- Program volunteer opportunities

### Emerging Major Donors ($5K-$9K)
- Phone check-ins (2-3x/year)
- Email updates (quarterly)
- Annual impact report
- Group cultivation events
- Pathway to higher engagement

---

## V. Communication Mix

### Personalized Touch Points
- Handwritten notes (minimum 4/year for top tiers)
- Birthday/anniversary recognition
- Holiday greetings
- Milestone celebrations

### Digital Communication
- Exclusive email newsletter
- Video impact updates
- Social media recognition (with permission)
- Virtual behind-the-scenes content

### Print Materials
- Annual reports with personalized covers
- Custom impact statements
- Program-specific publications
- Donor wall/recognition listings

---

## VI. Recognition Opportunities

### Naming Rights
- Buildings, rooms, programs, endowments
- Scholarships or fellowships
- Specific initiatives or campaigns

### Public Recognition
- Donor walls and plaques
- Annual report listings
- Website recognition
- Event programs
- Social media features (opt-in)

### Private Recognition
- Personal letters from beneficiaries
- Thank-you videos
- Impact photo albums
- Exclusive briefings

---

## VII. Impact Reporting Framework

### Quantitative Metrics
- Number of people served
- Programs funded/expanded
- Measurable outcomes achieved
- Leveraged funding attracted

### Qualitative Stories
- Beneficiary testimonials
- Program staff insights
- Before/after narratives
- Photos and videos

### Financial Transparency
- Gift allocation breakdown
- Program expense ratios
- Endowment performance (if applicable)
- Future sustainability plans

---

## VIII. Relationship Building Activities

### Exclusive Events
- Private dinners with leadership
- Site visit days
- Program launch celebrations
- Beneficiary meet-and-greets
- Strategic planning sessions

### Engagement Opportunities
- Advisory committee membership
- Volunteer experiences
- Mentor/mentee programs
- Peer-to-peer advocacy
- Special project collaboration

---

## IX. Moves Management Strategy

### Qualification
- Research capacity and interests
- Initial discovery conversations
- Alignment assessment

### Cultivation
- Multiple meaningful touchpoints
- Education about impact
- Relationship deepening
- Involvement opportunities

### Solicitation
- Tailored proposals
- Face-to-face asks
- Multi-year pledge options
- Legacy giving discussions

### Stewardship
- Everything in this plan
- Prepare for next gift

---

## X. Staff Roles & Responsibilities

### Executive Director/CEO
- Top 10-20 donor relationships
- Major solicitations
- Quarterly touchpoints
- Strategic relationship oversight

### Development Director
- Stewardship plan oversight
- Tier 2-3 relationship management
- Systems and tracking
- Staff coordination

### Program Staff
- Impact reporting content
- Site visits and tours
- Beneficiary connections
- Technical expertise sharing

### Board Members
- Peer relationships
- Event hosting
- Thank-you calls
- Strategic introductions

---

## XI. Metrics & Evaluation

### Track & Measure
- Donor retention rate by tier
- Upgrade rate (year-over-year)
- Engagement activity participation
- Satisfaction scores
- Average gift size trends
- Lifetime donor value
- Number of touchpoints per donor

### Annual Review
- Stewardship plan effectiveness
- Donor feedback integration
- Relationship health assessment
- Strategy adjustments needed

---

## XII. Tools & Systems

### CRM Requirements
- Contact history tracking
- Automated reminder systems
- Communication logging
- Relationship assignment tracking
- Custom reporting capabilities

### Documentation
- Stewardship contact reports
- Donor preference profiles
- Gift agreement files
- Recognition records

---

## XIII. Budget Considerations

### Allocate Funds For
- Event expenses (10-15% of gifts)
- Recognition materials
- Impact reporting production
- Travel for meetings
- Donor research tools
- Appreciation gifts (modest)

**General Rule**: Invest 10-20% of major gift revenue in stewardship activities

---

## XIV. Best Practices

### Do's
- ✓ Be authentic and genuine
- ✓ Listen more than you talk
- ✓ Follow through on commitments
- ✓ Respect donor preferences
- ✓ Share challenges honestly
- ✓ Celebrate donors appropriately
- ✓ Document everything

### Don'ts
- ✗ Only contact when asking for money
- ✗ Over-promise impact
- ✗ Neglect mid-year communication
- ✗ Use generic templates exclusively
- ✗ Forget to say thank you
- ✗ Ignore donor feedback

---

## XV. Continuous Improvement

- Quarterly stewardship audits
- Annual donor surveys
- Benchmark against peer organizations
- Stay current with best practices
- Regular staff training
- Adapt to donor feedback

---

**Remember**: Stewardship is an investment in long-term partnership, not a cost. Every dollar and minute spent building genuine relationships yields exponential returns in donor loyalty, advocacy, and giving.
